```{r}
source(paste0(dev_path, "dGCM_test.R"))
source(paste0(dev_path, "sieve.R"))
```

# Get data (or just load the provided data and move to the data analysis)
```{r}
# Define ticker symbols and names
# Market indices
index_tickers <- c("^GSPC", "^FTSE", "^HSI", "^N225")
index_names <- c("SP500", "FTSE100", "HangSeng", "Nikkei225")


# Define date range - daily returns for 2022-2025
start_date <- as.Date("2022-01-01")
end_date <- as.Date("2025-03-31")

# Function to download data and calculate daily returns
get_daily_returns <- function(ticker, asset_name) {
  # Try to download the data
  tryCatch({
    # Get data from Yahoo Finance
    asset_data <- getSymbols(ticker, src = "yahoo", 
                           from = start_date, 
                           to = end_date, 
                           auto.assign = FALSE)
    
    # Extract closing prices (Adjusted for indices)
    
    # For indices, use the Adjusted Close price (6th column)
    close_prices <- asset_data[, 6]
    
    colnames(close_prices) <- asset_name
    
    # Calculate log returns directly on daily data
    daily_returns <- diff(log(close_prices), lag = 1)
    
    # Replace NA with NA (just to make the first value NA, to be interpolated later)
    # The diff() function already creates an NA for the first value
    
    return(daily_returns)
  }, error = function(e) {
    message(paste("Error downloading data for", asset_name, ":", e$message))
    return(NULL)
  })
}

# Get daily returns for indices
index_returns_list <- list()
for (i in 1:length(index_tickers)) {
  index_returns_list[[index_names[i]]] <- get_daily_returns(index_tickers[i], index_names[i])
}

# Combine all returns into a single list
all_returns_list <- c(index_returns_list)

# Merge all returns into a single xts object
all_returns_xts <- do.call(merge, all_returns_list)

# Instead of removing NAs, use linear interpolation
# First create a complete date sequence to ensure all days are included
date_seq <- seq(min(index(all_returns_xts)), max(index(all_returns_xts)), by="day")
empty_xts <- xts(order.by=date_seq)

# Merge with empty time series to ensure all dates exist
all_returns_xts <- merge(all_returns_xts, empty_xts)

# Use linear interpolation for missing values
all_returns_xts_interp <- na.approx(all_returns_xts, na.rm=FALSE)

# For any remaining NAs at the start or end, use the next/previous value
all_returns_xts_interp <- na.locf(all_returns_xts_interp, fromLast = TRUE)
all_returns_xts_interp <- na.locf(all_returns_xts_interp)

# Check if there are still any NAs
any_na <- any(is.na(all_returns_xts_interp))
if(any_na) {
  cat("Warning: There are still some NA values in the dataset after interpolation.\n")
  # Replace any remaining NAs with zeros (this should be rare)
  all_returns_xts_interp[is.na(all_returns_xts_interp)] <- 0
}

# Convert xts object to dataframe with date column
all_returns <- data.frame(Date = index(all_returns_xts_interp), coredata(all_returns_xts_interp))

# Create visualizations with ggplot2
# Reshape data for plotting
indices_data <- melt(all_returns[, c("Date", index_names)], 
                    id.vars = "Date", variable.name = "Index", value.name = "Return")

all_returns <- all_returns %>% mutate(
    SP500_lag1 = lag(SP500),
    HangSeng_lag1 = lag(HangSeng),
    Nikkei225_lag1 = lag(Nikkei225),
    FTSE100_lag1 = lag(FTSE100)
  )
all_returns <- all_returns[-1,]

all_returns$const <- 1

all_returns$isWeekend <- weekdays(all_returns$Date) %in% c("Saturday", "Sunday")
df_all_returns <- all_returns[!all_returns$isWeekend,]
df_all_returns <- df_all_returns %>% select(-isWeekend)

# Save the final dataframe and all analysis data as RDS files
saveRDS(df_all_returns, paste0(data_path,"returns.rds")) # or save as csv with write.csv()
```

# Data analysis
```{r}
df <- readRDS(paste0(data_path,"returns.rds")) # or read csv with read.csv()
```

```{r}
# set seed for reproducibility
set.seed(2025) 

# Create a dataframe with columns X, Y, Z in the same order as the p-value variables
xyz_df <- data.frame(
  X = c(
    "SP500", "SP500", "SP500", "FTSE100", "FTSE100", "HangSeng",
    "SP500", "SP500", "SP500", "SP500", "SP500", "SP500",
    "FTSE100", "FTSE100", "FTSE100", "FTSE100", "HangSeng", "HangSeng",
    "FTSE100", "FTSE100", "Nikkei225", "FTSE100", "Nikkei225", "HangSeng"
  ),
  Y = c(
    "FTSE100", "HangSeng", "Nikkei225", "HangSeng", "Nikkei225", "Nikkei225",
    "FTSE100", "FTSE100", "HangSeng", "HangSeng", "Nikkei225", "Nikkei225",
    "HangSeng", "HangSeng", "Nikkei225", "Nikkei225", "Nikkei225", "Nikkei225",
    "Nikkei225", "HangSeng", "HangSeng", "SP500_lag1", "SP500_lag1", "SP500_lag1"
  ),
  Z = c(
    "const", "const", "const", "const", "const", "const",
    "HangSeng", "Nikkei225", "FTSE100", "Nikkei225", "FTSE100", "HangSeng",
    "SP500", "Nikkei225", "SP500", "HangSeng", "SP500", "FTSE100",
    "SP500_lag1", "SP500_lag1", "SP500_lag1", "const", "const", "const"
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# for minimum volatility method for selecting lag window for cov estimation
# lag window candidates to consider
n_sample <- nrow(df)
mv_seq_by <- 1 # consider contiguous lag window sizes, increments of 1
mv_num_neighbors <- 12 # for calculation of volatility criterion
power_lw <- 3 / 4 # power for largest candidate lag window size
lw_candidates <- seq(1, max(1, floor(n_sample^power_lw)), mv_seq_by)

# number of simulations for the Gaussian process for estimating quantile
n_boot <- 4999


# for sieve estimator grid (z,u)
n_esti <- 250

# significance level
alpha <- 0.05

# subsampling buffer for cross-validation
cv_buffer <- 1



for (i in 1:nrow(xyz_df)) {
    # SP500, FTSE100, HangSeng, Nikkei225
    # SP500_lag1
    # const
    x_name <- xyz_df$X[i] # name of X time series
    y_name <- xyz_df$Y[i] # name of Y time series
    z_name <- xyz_df$Z[i] # name of Z time series

    print(paste("i",i,"/",nrow(xyz_df)))
    print(paste("x_name",x_name))
    print(paste("y_name",y_name))
    print(paste("z_name",z_name))


    # grid of numbers of basis functions for the sieve estimator
    c_vec <- seq(2, 10, 2) # for time
    if(z_name == "const") {
      d_vec <- c(1) # for indep test
    } else {
      d_vec <- seq(2, 10, 2) # for covariate
    }

    cv_res_x <- cv_skip_sampling(regressors = data.frame(df[, z_name]), # nolint
                                regressand = df[, x_name],
                                c_vec = c_vec, d_vec = d_vec, b_time = "Legen",
                                b_timese = "Legen", mp_type = "algeb",
                                cv_buffer = cv_buffer,
                                s = 1, n_esti = n_esti)
    c_sieve_x <- cv_res_x$c_min_mse
    d_sieve_x <- cv_res_x$d_min_mse

    x_fitted <- esti_ts(regressors = data.frame(df[, z_name]), # nolint
                        regressand = df[, x_name],
                        c = c_sieve_x, d = d_sieve_x,
                        b_time = "Legen", b_timese = "Legen",
                        mp_type = "algeb", s = 1, n_esti = n_esti)

    cv_res_y <- cv_skip_sampling(regressors = data.frame(df[, z_name]), # nolint
                                regressand = df[, y_name],
                                c_vec = c_vec, d_vec = d_vec,
                                b_time = "Legen", b_timese = "Legen",
                                mp_type = "algeb", cv_buffer = cv_buffer,
                                s = 1, n_esti = n_esti)

    c_sieve_y <- cv_res_y$c_min_mse
    d_sieve_y <- cv_res_y$d_min_mse

    y_fitted <- esti_ts(regressors = data.frame(df[, z_name]), # nolint
                        regressand = df[, y_name],
                        c = c_sieve_y, d = d_sieve_y,
                        b_time = "Legen", b_timese = "Legen",
                        mp_type = "algeb", s = 1, n_esti = n_esti)
    x_resid <- df[, x_name] - x_fitted
    y_resid <- df[, y_name] - y_fitted


    res <- dgcm_test(x_on_z_resid = x_resid, # nolint
                        y_on_z_resid = y_resid,
                        lw_candidates = lw_candidates, mv_se_param = mv_num_neighbors, fp = data_path,
                        alpha = alpha, nsim = n_boot,
                        plot.residuals = FALSE)



    res["c_sieve_x"] <- c_sieve_x
    res["d_sieve_x"] <- d_sieve_x
    res["c_sieve_y"] <- c_sieve_y
    res["d_sieve_y"] <- d_sieve_y

    # Save the list as an RData file
    list.save(res, file = paste0(data_path, "res_stock_application","_x_",x_name,"_y_",y_name,"_z_",z_name,".RData"))


    # Set threshold or reference level
    threshold <- res$boot_quantile
    test_res <- data.frame(index = seq(n_sample), psum_proc = abs((cumsum(x_resid * y_resid))) / sqrt(n_sample))
    # Plot
    pres <- ggplot(test_res, aes(x = index, y = psum_proc)) +
    geom_line(color = "blue") +  # Time series line
    geom_hline(yintercept = threshold, color = "red", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1) +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(title = "Partial Sum Process and Quantile",
        y = "Value", x = "Time")

    ggsave(paste0(data_path,"dgcm_test_res_stock_application","_x_",x_name,"_y_",y_name,"_z_",z_name,".pdf"), plot = pres, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 300)
}
```
